properties.description: BL-188 and BL-191, built together because both are Artifact properties and a schema change costs the same for two as for one. THE SHARED FAILURE, which is why they are one capability rather than two: in each case the graph held two OPPOSITE states that produced an identical reading, and the tool reported the wrong one confidently. GRANULARITY (atomic / opaque / pending_expansion) — a directory Artifact claims its whole subtree, which is the adopt skill's own rule, so a registration check reported "every live doc is registered", truthfully, across 359 individually unreferenceable files, and coverage_report counted the directory as covering everything beneath it. A settled archive claimed on purpose and a placeholder nobody has got to yet were indistinguishable. coverage_report now returns pending_expansion and opaque_claims SEPARATELY, which makes "53 artifacts, of which 3 stand in for the rest" producible from the graph — a sentence that could not be formed at all before. Deliberately stores NO count of what a placeholder stands for: reflow2 does no file IO, so a stored number would be a caller-supplied figure nothing can recompute, the exact staleness BL-187 names. VOLATILITY (stable / append_only / living) — five coordination buses modelled with checksums, exactly per the adopt skill's instruction, produced five checksum_change divergences within minutes, all correct and all meaningless, with the disposition owed again on every reconcile forever. A content change on a volatile artifact now reports as expected_change and is not written to the drift ledger. IT IS REPORTED, NOT SUPPRESSED, and that is the load-bearing restraint: silence would trade a false positive for a false negative and let a wholesale replacement pass unmentioned, which is strictly the worse bug and the trap BL-176 was careful to avoid. Absence still fires at full severity whatever the volatility. SHRINK DETECTION IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT and stays open: a shrink is the genuinely alarming event for an append-only file, a checksum cannot express it, it needs a size baseline nothing records, and the reporting team's own compaction shrinks those files on purpose — so the heuristic needs the design's consent rather than a bare rule. BOTH VALUES ARE READ FROM THE NODE, NEVER INFERRED: no amount of looking at a tree recovers whether opacity was a decision, and no amount of hashing distinguishes a log that grew from a source file that was edited. Written by set_artifact_intent, a dedicated setter rather than arguments on add_artifact, because a constructor taking a partial property set and writing the whole node erases what the caller did not name (BL-183). Adding the properties without a tool to write them would have created two more properties reachable from nothing, which is BL-202's exact defect.
properties.name: An artifact declares what it stands for and how its content behaves, so a report can tell two opposite states apart
